title: Kernel + Prefetch scratchpad — midweek sync
content:
Purpose:
Quick midweek brain-dump from the kernel/prefetch pairing session. This is intentionally informal — notes, open questions, micro-benchmarks, and next-step todos.

Attendees:
- Liang, Asha, Marco, Priya, Evan
- ~15m adhoc followups with SRE and infra later

High-level goal:
- Reduce tail latency for interactive chat workloads while keeping token-cost within target. Primary levers: smarter prefetch (prefix caching + speculative KV warming) and tighter micro-batching windows, with conservative kernel changes staged behind feature flags.

What we tried this week (summary):
1) Speculative prefetch shim in front of KV store (prototype):
   - Idea: when incoming request looks like continuation (same convo id or same model + user hash), spawn async prefetch for likely next-key ranges using last-N tokens heuristic.
   - Implementation: lightweight goroutine in the request path that issues non-blocking GetRange requests to KV cache with low-priority QoS.
   - Result: median token latency improved ~3–6% for warm sessions in our 99q test harness. Tail (p95-p99) improved by 8–12% when prefetch hit rate > 40%.
   - Cost: extra background RPCs increased network IO modestly; CPU bump on nodes handling prefetch threads (~4%).

2) Batching window tuning experiment (0–30ms windows):
   - Observed throughput vs latency tradeoff: 5–10ms window gives best throughput uplift without harming 95th too much; 20ms reduces latency wins but increases p99 significantly for short-response models.
   - For long-seq models, larger windows are more beneficial. We need per-model window config rather than global.

3) Kernel fallback policy test (retry path):
   - Added soft-fallback to older kernel if new kernel kernel_O1 times out beyond threshold. Measured small improvement in perceived availability but added complexity in metrics (double counting tokens).

Open questions / concerns:
- Prefetch correctness: we must ensure speculative prefetch never leaks cross-tenant state. Current prototype uses tenant-scoped keys and honors ACL checks but ask security to sign-off.
- Eviction interplay: prefetch increases cache churn. When eviction policy is LRU, we see thrash for large numbers of small sessions. Maybe use segmented LRU or TTL-based pinning for prefetched segments.
- Cost model: need to account for additional RPCs in unit econ (per-token + prefetch overhead). Early estimate: 1.03x token CPU for 40% prefetch hit rate.
- Rollout safety: kernel feature flag + canary in one AZ, route 1% traffic, monitor p95/p99, token counters, and evictions. If evictions spike > 15% rollback.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Keep prefetch behind feature flag; enable for internal perf tests only until security sign-off.
- Implement per-model batching window config in config service rather than hardcoded constant. Marco to draft config schema.
- Add a new eviction metric (prefetch_eviction_ratio) and a dashboard tile. Priya to own dashboard.

Short action list (owners and rough ETA):
- Asha: Add tenant-scope assertions and add small unit test suite for prefetch correctness (ETA: 2026-05-12).
- Marco: Design per-model batching config schema + migration plan for existing routes (ETA: 2026-05-14).
- Priya: Dashboards — create prefetch_eviction_ratio and per-kernel token counter (ETA: 2026-05-10).
- Evan: Hook feature-flag gating into rollout pipeline + create az-canary job (ETA: 2026-05-11).
- Liang: Run cost-model sim for prefetch at 10/20/40/60% hit rates and share spreadsheet (ETA: 2026-05-09).

Micro-benchmarks (quick numbers from local staging harness):
- Baseline (no prefetch, batching 5ms): median token latency 12.4ms, p95 27.8ms, p99 45.2ms
- With spec-prefetch (hit=45%), batching 5ms: median 11.7ms, p95 25.0ms, p99 39.0ms
- Batching 20ms (no prefetch): median 10.9ms, p95 40.1ms, p99 82.5ms (bad for short models)
- Kernel fallback enabled: availability improved +0.7% in synthetic flakiness tests but token accounting requires fix

Notes-to-self / brainstorm snippets:
- Could we combine prefetch with hint signals from router (e.g., if UI sends 'typing' event, warm next keys aggressively)?
- Consider cheap probabilistic bloom keys that indicate likely continuation prefixes rather than full KV fetches to reduce churn.
- TTL pinning for prefetched keys for N seconds to reduce eviction thrash; test with adaptive TTL based on recent hit-rate.
- If kernel change increases L2 cache misses, throttled prefetching might reduce the negative impact: start small and ramp with hit rate feedback loop.

Blockers:
- Security sign-off for speculative prefetch (Priya to ping security).
- Observability gap: we don't have easy per-tenant eviction tracing yet — will make debug slow.

Meeting follow-ups / suggested agenda for next sync:
- Review Priya dashboard mock and agree on alert thresholds (p95 jump, eviction ratio > 0.15).
- Marco to present per-model batching config options and how to store defaults in model catalog.
- Asha to demo prefetch unit tests and results of small-scale internal canary.

Misc notes:
- Customer impact: early internal perf tests indicate users with long-lived sessions (assistant-like products) benefit the most. Short query apps risk higher p99 if batching window misconfigured.
- Keep docs lightweight in repo: add README under /docs/prefetch-experiments with how to reproduce harness.

If anything missing or inaccurate, leave inline comments here. This doc is a rough operational notebook; once we converge on the rollout plan I'll convert to a PRD style doc and move the checklist into the release-plan template.

-- Liang
summary: Midweek informal notes for kernel + prefetch experiments: prototype results, decisions to gate behind feature flag, action items with owners and ETAs, micro-bench numbers, open security/observability blockers, and follow-up agenda.
